prompt: How is AI currently positioned in institutional decision-making?
Which institutional decisions have actually changed in the last 18 months because of AI or anticipated AI-driven changes?
Which assumptions underlying the current institutional model could be materially affected by AI in the next 3–5 years?
When a significant external change is detected, what normally happens from detection to institutional action?
How many AI pilots were conducted, evaluated, scaled or stopped in the last 24 months?
A major AI development threatens a major programme within three years. What would the institution do first, who initiates it, and through what mechanism?
What distinctive institutional value does the university intend to strengthen as AI makes information and routine content increasingly abundant?
A new AI system processing student information is proposed. Who can authorise institutional deployment?
What steps actually occur before a consequential AI system is approved?
Which AI governance policies are approved, implemented and reviewed?
An AI system produces a harmful or discriminatory outcome affecting a student. What happens next?
For approved AI tools, how many process personal/student data and how many have undergone defined privacy/data review?
How does the institution determine whether student generative-AI use is appropriate?
For consequential AI-assisted decisions, where can a human review or override the output?
For the three most consequential external AI systems, what due diligence and monitoring has occurred?
Has the institution tested its AI governance process? What changed as a result?
Which graduate capabilities does the institution explicitly intend students to develop in the AI era?
For representative programmes, where is each selected capability intended, developed, demonstrated and assessed?
Provide one representative student activity/work sample demonstrating each of 3–5 selected capabilities.
How are students required to demonstrate capability rather than simply produce an answer?
Where are students expected to verify, challenge or contextualise AI-generated output?
How often do students work on unfamiliar or ambiguous problems with no single prepared answer?
Where available, what proportion of students meet defined competency thresholds for selected capabilities?
For non-technical disciplines, how are students developing AI capability relevant to their discipline?
Which three graduate capabilities are least convincingly demonstrated today, and what evidence led to that conclusion?
When a programme changes because the discipline or work environment is changing, what most often triggers the change?
For a representative programme, where are the capabilities students will need in five years deliberately developed and where are they actually demonstrated?
A core task taught in a programme can now be performed reliably by AI. How would the institution decide whether to retain it, redesign it, or remove it from the learning experience?
How quickly can a programme respond when external evidence shows that a major graduate capability or learning component needs to change?
Select 3–5 programmes and identify one meaningful change made because of AI, changing professional practice, or changing learner/work requirements. What evidence shows the change is real?
Where are faculty currently using AI in their actual academic work, and what is the most meaningful change it has produced?
After faculty receive AI-related development, what usually happens to the practice they were expected to change?
If an AI system can perform a significant part of an activity faculty currently teach, what would you expect the faculty member to change in the learning experience?
Which parts of academic work are changing because of AI, and how is the institution supporting faculty through those changes?
Provide a representative example of faculty practice where AI has improved, challenged or changed teaching, assessment or research—and show how the institution learned from it.
When students use AI for learning, what does the institution expect them to be able to do themselves before the work can be considered credible?
A student submits a polished AI-generated answer. What would you need to see to determine whether the student actually understands and can defend the work?
How often are students required to apply knowledge to unfamiliar, ambiguous or real situations where AI can assist but cannot simply supply the finished answer?
How is the institution helping students understand changing work requirements and build credible evidence of capability for employers, further study or entrepreneurship?
Which student groups are least able to access or benefit from AI-enabled learning, and what has the institution actually done in response?
Across representative programmes, what do students actually have to demonstrate to complete major assessments?
If generative AI could produce a plausible answer to a major assessment today, what would still make the assessment academically meaningful?
How does the institution know that students possess the capabilities its programmes say they develop?
How often are students asked to solve unfamiliar or ambiguous problems where there is no prepared model answer?
When assessment evidence shows students are weak in an important capability, what normally happens?
If leadership needs a reliable answer about students, programmes, faculty, placements or research today, how quickly can the institution produce it?
What normally happens to an important institutional data point from its creation to its use in a decision?
Which institutional capabilities are currently sufficient to support responsible AI-enabled academic or administrative use?
Give one recent leadership decision where institutional data or analytics materially changed the decision.
How does the institution identify what employers and professional sectors will expect from graduates over the next 3–5 years?
For a representative programme, how clearly can the institution connect intended graduate capabilities to actual occupational or professional requirements?
Where AI is changing entry-level work in a major sector relevant to the institution, what has the institution changed for students?
What evidence does the institution use to determine whether recruiters trust the capabilities of its graduates?
What research questions or themes does the institution believe will matter most to its disciplines, region or society over the next 5–10 years?
Take one significant research activity. What happened after the research generated a meaningful finding?
When a major problem crosses disciplinary boundaries, how does the institution bring the required expertise together?
Where AI is used in research, how does the institution protect research quality, provenance, integrity and human judgement?
How are students enabled to move from consuming existing knowledge to creating new knowledge, prototypes, evidence or solutions?
When a development could materially affect the institution, what normally happens between first awareness and an institutional response?
If leadership decides that an emerging capability has become strategically important, how can resources actually be redirected?
When an important institutional experiment does not work, what usually happens?

Which statement best describes the institution today?
